questions.q: What does the Fixed Assets to General Ledger transfer actually do?
options: It calculates depreciation for the current period
It moves accounted journal entry data from Assets into GL as an unposted journal batch
It retires assets automatically
It deletes journal entries from Assets
questions.explain: The transfer moves journal entries created by Create Accounting from the Assets subledger into GL, where they arrive as an unposted batch.

questions.q: What is the difference between transferring and posting?
options: They are the same action with different names
Transfer moves data into GL as an unposted batch; post is the separate GL action that updates account balances
Posting happens before transferring, never after
Transfer only applies to tax books
questions.explain: A transferred batch exists in GL but hasn't changed account balances yet; posting is the distinct step that actually updates those balances.

questions.q: What is a tradeoff of transferring Fixed Assets journal entries to GL only at period end rather than more frequently?
options: There is no tradeoff; frequency never matters
GL's fixed-asset balances will lag behind what Assets shows throughout the month
Period-end-only transfer is always faster to process
Period-end-only transfer prevents any reconciliation from being possible
questions.explain: Transferring only at period end means GL's picture of fixed assets lags behind Assets' own data until the transfer runs, a deliberate tradeoff against more frequent processing.

questions.q: If Assets and GL appear to disagree on a fixed-asset account balance, what should typically be checked first?
options: Whether the asset's category was deleted
Whether a batch is transferred but not yet posted, or accounted but not yet transferred
Whether the asset has ever been retired
Whether the depreciation method is flat-rate or straight-line
questions.explain: Apparent disagreements between Assets and GL are often explained by timing — a batch pending posting or pending transfer — rather than an actual error.

questions.q: Why does the two-step transfer-then-post design exist in the General Ledger?
options: To give GL its own checkpoint to review journals from any subledger before posting changes balances
To prevent Assets from ever creating journal entries
Because GL cannot process journal entries from subledgers directly
To automatically reverse all subledger transactions
questions.explain: Separating transfer from posting lets journals from any subledger be reviewed in GL before they actually change reported account balances.
